courses.title: General Chemistry for Engineers
courses.description: Provides engineering students with a background in pertinent concepts and principles of chemistry. Topics include atomic theory of structure and bonding, stoichiometry, gases, equilibrium, oxidation-reduction, electrochemistry, thermodynamics, and reaction kinetics, and their applications to engineering.
courses.prerequisites: C or better MAT 105, MAT 106, MAT 112, MAT 114, MAT 115, MAT 116, MAT 120, MAT 125, MAT 130, MAT 191, MAT 214, MAT 216, MAT 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, STA 1200 , SAT Math>=550, or ACT Math>=23.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: Engineering, Society, and You
courses.description: The development of the individual in society from an engineering perspective. The study of the integration of society and technology. Development includes introduction to the fields of engineering and engineering technology, career planning, development of a community of learners, critical thinking, problem solving skills, and ethical and professional behavior. Analysis of typical problems involving technology in society and their solutions. Guest speakers. Exposure to campus resources and provides a framework for developing and implementing an academic plan culminating in the award of a four-year degree.

courses.title: Engineering, Society, and You Laboratory
courses.description: The development of the individual in society from an engineering perspective. The study of the integration of society and technology. Development includes introduction to the fields of engineering and engineering technology, career planning, development of a community of learners, critical thinking, problem solving skills, and ethical and professional behavior. Analysis of typical problems involving technology in society and their solutions. Guest speakers. Exposure to campus resources and provides a framework for developing and implementing an academic plan culminating in the award of a four-year degree.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Ethical Concepts in Technology and Applied Science
courses.description: [GE 3C or 5D] Explores ethics of engineers, scientists, and others involved with technology related to values, philosophy, ethical theory and practice, moral reasoning, morality in law and codes, professional standards, and societies-case studies. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing

courses.title: Fiscal Implications in Technical Decision Making
courses.description: [GE 4C or 5D] Economic theory of capital allocation decisions. Current and relevant views of managerial economics used to present a unified theory of capital allocation appropriate to private, public and governmental entities. Integrated application of economic and operations analysis to managerial problem-solving and decision-making processes. Study of inflation and tax consequences on economic decisions. Open to all majors.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: [GE 2] Integration techniques including integration by parts, integrals of trigonometric products, partial fractions, substitution and trigonometric substitution. Hyperbolic functions. Improper Integrals, sequences and series, polar coordinates, parametric equations and conic sections.
courses.prerequisites: AP Calc AB >=3, AP Calc BC >=3, or C or better in MAT 1140 or MAT 1140C.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.description: Introduction to vectors, dot product, cross product, equations of lines and planes, calculus of vector valued functions, introduction to multivariable functions, differential calculus of multivariable functions, the chain rule, applications including extreme problems and Lagrange multipliers, integral calculus of multivariable functions, double and triple integrals, applications of double and triple integrals, line and surface integrals of vector fields, Green’s Theorem, the Divergence Theorem, Stokes’ Theorem.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 or MAT 1150C.

courses.title: Elementary Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
courses.description: Separable and linear ordinary differential equations; numerical and analytical solutions. Linear algebra: vectors in n-space, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization; applications to the study of systems of linear differential equations.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 or MAT 1150C.

courses.title: Engineering Graphics and Visualization Laboratory
courses.description: Engineering graphics & visualization for product design & manufacturing. Drafting methods & techniques including multiview orthographic projection, isometrics and pictorials, sections & auxiliary views, dimensioning and tolerancing. Drafting and sketching using instruments and CAD.
courses.prerequisites: ME major.

courses.title: Computer-Aided Computations
courses.description: Problems involving basic computational methods including elementary concepts of computer programming. Proficiency will be gained in writing computer programs to solve engineering problems. Assignments include the use of the computer facilities. Assignments include the use of the computer facilities. Corequisite(s): ME 1101L .
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 114, MAT 1140 , or MAT 1140C.

courses.title: Computer-Aided Computations Laboratory
courses.description: Problems involving basic computational methods including elementary concepts of computer programming. Proficiency will be gained in writing computer programs to solve engineering problems. Assignments include the use of the computer facilities. Corequisite(s): ME 1101 .
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 114, MAT 1140 , or MAT 1140C.

courses.title: Vector Statics
courses.description: Two and three dimensional equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies including frames, machines and trusses employing vector algebra. Principles of friction, centroids and centers of gravity, mass and area moments of inertia. Shear and moment diagrams for beams.
courses.prerequisites: ME major; C or better in MAT 1140 or MAT 114; and C- or better in the following: PHY 1510 or PHY 131, and PHY 1510L or PHY 131L.

courses.title: Vector Dynamics
courses.description: Cross Listed as: ARO 2150 Vector mathematics of absolute and relative motion of particles and the planar motion of rigid bodies in an inertial reference frame using Cartesian, Normal and Tangential and Polar Coordinate Systems; Newton’s laws of motion, work-energy, linear and angular impulse momentum, direct and oblique central impact.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 2141 or ME 214, or C or better in ARO 2041 or CE 2041 ; and C or better in MAT 1150 , MAT 1150C, or MAT 116.

courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Strength and elastic deflection of engineering materials due to loads applied axially, in torsion, in bending, and in shear. Normal Stress-Strain diagrams, Shear Stress-Strain Diagrams, Generalized Hookâ€™s Law, Mohrâ€™s Circle; deflection and slope of beams by double integration, stresses on oblique planes, statically indeterminate members under axial, torsional and bending loads; combined stresses and principal stresses.
courses.prerequisites: ME major, and C- or better in ME 2141 or ME 214.

courses.title: Introduction to Design Laboratory
courses.description: Project-based lab focusing on hands-on independent and team design projects. Systematic approach to engineering design: concept generation, prototyping, and testing. Emphasizing multidisciplinary engineering, technical communication, and creative problem-solving.
courses.prerequisites: ME major and C- or better in the following: ME 1001L , or MFE 126 and MFE 126L; and ME 2141 or ME 214.

courses.title: Circuit Analysis For Mechanical Engineers
courses.description: Analysis of electrical components and circuits. Ohmâ€™s law, Kirchoffâ€™s Laws, ThÃ©venin and Norton Theorems, diode characteristics. Properties of 1st order low-pass and high-pass filters. Time-domain analysis of 2nd order circuits. Corequisite(s): ME 2401L .
courses.prerequisites: ME major and C- or better in PHY 1520 , PHY 1520L , and MAT 2240 .

courses.title: Circuit Analysis For Mechanical Engineers Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on practices related to electrical components and circuits analysis, Ohmâ€™s law, Kirchoffâ€™s Laws, properties of 1st order low-pass and high-pass filters. Laboratory measurement of electrical quantities such as voltage and current. Multimeter, oscilloscope, and function generator operation in conjunction with virtual electronics analysis environment. Corequisite(s): ME 2401 .
courses.prerequisites: ME major and C- or better in PHY 1520 , PHY 1520L , and MAT 2240 .

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Thermodynamic properties and processes; equations of state; tables and charts of thermodynamic properties; work and heat, the first law of thermodynamics and first law properties; the second law of thermodynamics and entropy; gas power cycles.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ARO 2041 , CE 2041 , ME 2141 , or ME 214.

courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Analysis and problems dealing with properties and behavior of fluids at rest and in motion. Fundamental concepts; fluid statics; transport theorem; flow of incompressible frictionless fluid; laminar and turbulent flow of real fluids in closed conduits; impulse and momentum applied to fluids; Similarity and dimensional analysis; steady closed conduit flow in series, parallel and branching pipes; pump/pipe networks; pump characteristics.
courses.prerequisites: Mechanical Engineering major, C or better in MAT 2140 or MAT 214, and C- or better in ME 2150 or ME 215.

courses.title: Intermediate Thermal-Fluids Engineering
courses.description: Thermo/fluids measurements; Vapor and combined power cycles; Refrigeration cycles; Thermodynamic property relations; Mixtures of ideal and real gases; Psychrometric chart; Combustion; Boundary layers, drag and lift; Compressible flow.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ME 3011 , or ME 301; and ME 3111 , or ME 312.

courses.title: Thermal-Fluids Laboratory
courses.description: Measurement of viscosity of fluids, centrifugal pump and/or fan performance, turbine performance, pressure drop in pipe systems, flow rate meters, jet momentum, air velocity distribution in ducts, air conditioning and refrigeration systems, dimensional analysis, oxygen bomb calorimetry, steam power cycle, and heat exchanger. Proficiency will be gained in the calibration and use of laboratory equipment, design of basic fluid mechanics and thermodynamics experiments, the acquisition, processing, and analysis of data by manual and automated methods, and report writing. Corequisite(s): ME 3121 or ME 312.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Engineering Materials
courses.description: A study of the relationship among structure, processing and properties of engineering materials; strengthening mechanisms for ferrous and non-ferrous metals and the application of such materials in engineering situations; phase diagrams and their relevance to the structure, processing and properties of metallic alloys; mechanical behavior of polymers, ceramics and composites and their applications in engineering practice; corrosion and degradation of materials; introduction to nanomaterials.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 1150 , CHM 1210 , or CHM 121; and C- or better in ME 2191 or ME 218.

courses.title: Stress Analysis
courses.description: Thin and thick-walled pressurized cylinders, rotating rings, thermal stress, press and shrink fits, curved beams, contact stresses. Deflections of beams by singularity functions and superposition, strain energy, Castiglianoâ€™s theorem, statically indeterminate problems, buckling, experimental stress analysis, and other special topics. Failure theories, stress concentration, steady and repeated loading. Fatigue and endurance strength. Corequisite(s): ME 3150 and ME 3501L .
courses.prerequisites: Mechanical Engineering major and C- or better in the following: ME 2191 or ME 219, and ME 2331L or ME 233L.

courses.title: Machine Design
courses.description: Design and application of machine components such as shaft, threaded fasteners, springs, brakes, clutches, gears, flexible machine elements, and bearings. Lubrication of machine elements. Design techniques and design methodology of a machine. Project management. Corequisite(s): ME 3250L .
courses.prerequisites: ME major; MFE 2010 or MFE 201; MFE 2010L or MFE 201L; and C- or better in the following: ME 2150 or ME 215, and ME 3190 or ME 319.

courses.title: Machine Design Laboratory
courses.description: Design and application of machine components such as brakes, clutches, gears, flexible machine elements, and bearings. Lubrication of machine elements. Design techniques and design of a simple machine. Corequisite(s): ME 3250 .
courses.prerequisites: MFE 2010 or MFE 201; MFE 2010L or MFE 201L; and C- or better in the following: ME 2150 or ME 215, and ME 3190 or ME 319.

courses.title: Synthesis of Mechanical Engineering Problems
courses.description: Analysis and synthesis of steady-state and transient-state mechanical engineering problems. Topics include: ordinary differential equations, Laplace Transform, Fourier series, partial differential equations, and probability and statistics (uncertainty analysis, random sampling, hypothesis testing).
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 2240 , MAT 216, or MAT 224; and ME major.

courses.title: Mechanics, Behavior and Selection of Materials Laboratory
courses.description: Standard physical tests of engineering materials including torsion, tension, compression and bending. Experimental stress analysis using strain gages. Examination of the effects of cold working, annealing, and heat treatment on the mechanical properties of materials. Experiments involving galvanic corrosion and behavior of polymers and ceramics under load. Experiments on creep of polymers and metals. Material selection for prescribed applications. Corequisite(s): ME 3150 or ME 315.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: Analysis and synthesis of steady-state and transient engineering problems associated with stiffness and influence coefficients, shape functions, element stiffness, coordinate transformations, and assembling of stiffness matrix. Solution to give deflections and forces, or analogous parameters for heat transfer and fluid flows. Apply a widely-used finite element computer program (NASTRAN) to structure design, heat transfer and/or fluid flow. Corequisite(s): ME 4060A .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3401 or ME 340, and ME 3190 or ME 319.

courses.title: Finite Element Analysis Activity
courses.description: Analysis and synthesis of steady-state and transient engineering problems associated with stiffness and influence coefficients, shape functions, element stiffness, coordinate transformations, and assembling of stiffness matrix. Solution to give deflections and forces, or analogous parameters for heat transfer and fluid flows. Apply a widely-used finite element computer program (NASTRAN) to structure design, heat transfer and/or fluid flow. Corequisite(s): ME 4060 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ME 3401 or ME 340, and ME 3190 or ME 319.

courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description: Basic principles of conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer. One-dimensional and multi-dimensional conduction, steady and unsteady state. Theoretical and empirical relations for free and forced convection in external surface flows and in internal flows. Basic laws of radiation heat transfer, radiation properties of surfaces and radiant energy exchange among simple surfaces. Corequisite(s): ME 3121 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: MAT 2240 , MAT 216, or MAT 224; ME 3011 or ME 301; and ME 3111 or ME 311.

courses.title: Thermal Systems Design
courses.description: Preliminary design and preparation of specifications for procurement of thermal fluid mechanical equipment to meet performance requirements. Projects
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ME 3121 or ME 312, and ME 4150 or ME 415.

courses.title: Mechanical Measurements
courses.description: Analysis of the generalized measurement system with application of sensing, signal conditioning and data acquisition to problems of engineering measurements. Uncertainty Analysis, First- and Second-order system models, Transfer functions, Time- and Frequency-domain Analysis, Bode Diagrams, Dynamic Signals, Filters, Sensors. Corequisite(s): ME 4351L .
courses.prerequisites: ME major and C- or better in ME 2401 , ME 2401L , ME 3131L , and ME 3401 .

courses.title: Mechanical Measurements Laboratory
courses.description: Analysis of the generalized measurement system with application of sensing, signal conditioning and data acquisition to problems of engineering measurements. Uncertainty Analysis, First- and Second-order system models, Transfer functions, Time- and Frequency-domain Analysis, Bode Diagrams, Dynamic Signals, Filters, Sensors. Corequisite(s): ME 4351 .
courses.prerequisites: ME major and C- or better in ME 2401 , ME 2401L , ME 3131L , and ME 3401 .

courses.title: Control of Mechanical Systems
courses.description: Feedback control system design and analysis. Stability criteria, root locus plots, transfer functions, introduction to feedback control and microprocessor applications. Frequency response, Bode Plots, frequency domain stability design. Concepts of PID controller tuning. Programming of control systems using microprocessors. Corequisite(s): ME 4391L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 4351 and ME 4351L or ME 435 and ME 435L.

courses.title: Control of Mechanical Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Feedback control system design and analysis. Stability criteria, root locus plots, transfer functions, introduction to feedback control and microprocessor applications. Frequency response, Bode Plots, frequency domain stability design. Concepts of PID controller tuning. Programming of control systems using microprocessors. Corequisite(s): ME 4391 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 4351 and ME 4351L , or ME 435 and ME 435L.

courses.title: Manufacturing Systems and Processes
courses.description: Study of basic manufacturing processes with emphasis on terminology, technology, process principles and capabilities, material selection and comparative advantages and disadvantages. Processes discussed include material removal, joining, assembly, 3D printing and casting. Other topics include NC, measurement and gaging, and statistical methods. Corequisite(s): MFE 2010L .

courses.title: Manufacturing Systems and Processes Laboratory
courses.description: Study of basic manufacturing processes with emphasis on terminology, technology, process principles and capabilities, material selection and comparative advantages and disadvantages. Processes discussed include material removal, joining, assembly, 3D printing and casting. Other topics include NC, measurement and gaging, and statistical methods. Corequisite(s): MFE 2010 .

courses.title: Introduction to Newtonian Mechanics
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to mechanics, including Newton’s laws, vectors, statics, kinematics, conservation laws, rotational motion, Newtonian gravity, fluids, and simple harmonic motion. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 115, MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ( MAT 1150 can be concurrent).

courses.title: Newtonian Mechanics Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Experiments in Newtonian mechanics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Introduction to Electromagnetism and Circuits
courses.description: Introduction to electricity and magnetism, including electrostatics, dc circuits, magnetostatics, electrodynamics, and Maxwell’s equations. Corequisite(s): PHY 1520L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 115 or MAT 1150 ; and C- or better in PHY 132, PHY 132B, PHY 1510B or PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Introductory Laboratory on Electromagnetism and Circuits
courses.description: Experiments in electricity and magnetism. Corequisite(s): PHY 1520 .

courses.title: Alternative Energy Systems
courses.description: Analysis and synthesis of energy systems, their interconnectedness and impact on the environment and society. Topics include solar, geothermal, wind, biomass, hydro and ocean resources, electrochemical energy systems, conversion, storage, and distribution.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHE 3021 , ME 3011 , or ME 301.

courses.title: Acoustics and Noise Control
courses.description: Wave equation, fundamental acoustic parameters (Lp , Lw , LI ), noise criteria and regulations, noise source, noise measurement, noise absorption and transmission, room acoustics, noise suppression by absorption, isolation and resonators. Case studies in noise control and reduction.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3111 or ME 311, ME 4351 or ME 435, and ME 4351L or ME 435L.

courses.title: Solar Thermal Engineering
courses.description: Solar radiation distribution and measurement; methods of solar energy collection; thermal analysis of flat plate solar collectors; experimental testing and efficiency determination; solar energy economics; transient and long-term system performance; photovoltaics (PV); computer modeling for solar and water heating applications. Corequisite(s): ME 4070L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 4150 or ME 415.

courses.title: Solar Thermal Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Solar radiation distribution and measurement; methods of solar energy collection; thermal analysis of flat plate solar collectors; experimental testing and efficiency determination; solar energy economics; transient and long-term system performance; photovoltaics (PV); computer modeling for solar and water heating applications. Corequisite(s): ME 4070 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 4150 or ME 415.

courses.title: Nuclear Engineering
courses.description: Nuclear power plant design, operation and safety, reactor vessel internal and core components, nuclear physics, neutron reactions, fission and moderation; reactor physics and reactor kinetics.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 2240 , MAT 216, or MAT 224; and C- or better in the following: PHY 1520 or PHY 133; and ME 3011 or ME 301.

courses.title: Heat Power
courses.description: Application of the principles of thermodynamics to actual power plant cycles. Rankine cycle and its variations; boiler and steam turbine heat balance and efficiency; steam plant auxiliaries; plant heat balance and efficiency; gas turbine and combined cycles. Corequisite(s): ME 4110L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3121 , or ME 302 and ME 311.

courses.title: Heat Power Laboratory
courses.description: Application of the principles of thermodynamics to actual power plant cycles. Rankine cycle and its variations; boiler and steam turbine heat balance and efficiency; steam plant auxiliaries; plant heat balance and efficiency; gas turbine and combined cycles. Corequisite(s): ME 4110 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3121 , or ME 302 and ME 311.

courses.title: Internal Combustion Engines
courses.description: The development of analytical and experimental techniques to estimate the performance of internal combustion engines. Discussion includes ideal and actual cycles, combustion, carburetion, fuel injection, ignition, supercharging, cooling, and fuels as applied to spark ignition and compression ignition engines. Corequisite(s): ME 4120L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3121 or ME 302.

courses.title: Internal Combustion Engines Laboratory
courses.description: The development of analytical and experimental techniques to estimate the performance of internal combustion engines. Discussion includes ideal and actual cycles, combustion, carburetion, fuel injection, ignition, supercharging, cooling, and fuels as applied to spark ignition and compression ignition engines. Corequisite(s): ME 4120 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3121 or ME 302.

courses.title: Mechanical Vibrations
courses.description: Rotating unbalance, vibration isolation, vibration measuring instruments, vibration of multiple degree of freedom systems, normal modes analysis, flexibility and stiffness coefficients, transfer matrices, computational methods, the finite element method and continuous systems. Additional special topics selected by the instructor.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3401 or ME 340, and C- or better in ME 2150.

courses.title: Intermediate Dynamics
courses.description: Three-dimensional particle dynamics and rigid body kinematics, motion relative to rotating reference frames, moments and products of inertia, momentum and energy principles, rotating shafts, gyroscopic motion, free tumbling motion, virtual work, Hamilton’s principle, Lagrange dynamics.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 2240 , MAT 216, or MAT 224; and C- or better in ME 2150 or ME 215.

courses.title: Air Conditioning
courses.description: Thermodynamic processes in buildings, thermal review of psychrometrics; building psychometric processes; comfort and air quality; building air distribution systems; principles of refrigeration; refrigeration equipment; heating equipment; air conditioning system types; contemporary topics on building energy efficiency and green building design and simulation. Corequisite(s): ME 4180L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ME 3121 , or ME 302 and ME 312; and ME 4150 or ME 415.

courses.title: Air Conditioning Laboratory
courses.description: Thermodynamic processes in buildings, thermal Review of psychrometrics; building psychometric processes; comfort and air quality; building air distribution systems; principles of refrigeration; refrigeration equipment; heating equipment; air conditioning system types; Contemporary topics on building energy efficiency and green building design and simulation; Use of industry standard software TRACE 3D Plus to complete team course design projects. Corequisite(s): ME 4180 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ME 3121 , or ME 302 and ME 312; and ME 4150 or ME 415.

courses.title: Dynamics of Machinery
courses.description: Type synthesis and number synthesis. Path, function and motion generation mechanisms. Quick return, dwell and straight line mechanisms. Intermittent motion. Graphical synthesis of linkage mechanisms. 4-bar and six-bar mechanisms. Position, velocity and acceleration analysis of mechanisms by graphical, analytical and computer techniques. Instant center. Mechanical advantage. Determination of static and dynamic forces on linkages. CAM design and analysis. Compliant mechanisms. Balancing of rotating masses. Critical speeds of shafts. Analysis of gyroscopic action with applications.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 2150 or ME 215.

courses.title: Mechanics of Composite Materials
courses.description: An introduction to composite materials; relationship between the properties of the constituents and those of composite materials; empirical equations used to determine the strength and stiffness properties of Fiber Reinforced Composites (FRCs); mechanics of orthotropic materials, analysis of fiber reinforced composite lamina, lamination theory and its application in Fiber Reinforced Composites; hygrothermal effects; design methodology and design for stiffness and strength, use of carpet plots and simplified design methods.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3150 or ME 315; C- or better in ME 3190 or ME 319; and C or better in MAT 2240 , MAT 216, or MAT 224.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Design and Analysis
courses.description: The role and usage of analysis in design, engineering judgment of students in the idealization and modelling of real machine components and structures. Evaluation of machine structures quickly and efficiently, using both classical hand analysis and finite element analysis methods. Corequisite(s): ME 4251L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ME 3250 or ME 325, and ME 3250L or ME 325L.

courses.title: Advanced Machine Design and Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: The role and usage of analysis in design, seeking to hone the engineering judgment of students in the idealization and modelling of real machine components and structures, such that students will be able to evaluate machine structures quickly and efficiently, using both classical hand analysis and finite element analysis methods and comparing their results. Corequisite(s): ME 4251 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ME 3250 or ME 325, and ME 3250L or ME 325L.

courses.title: Engineering Computational Methods
courses.description: Numerical techniques applied to engineering problems including solving systems of linear equations, finding roots of non-linear equations, numerical integration and differentiation, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations, and curve fitting.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 2240 , MAT 216, or MAT 224; and C- or better in ME 1101 and ME 1101L , or ME 232.

courses.title: Air Pollution Formation and Control
courses.description: Atmosphere characteristics; Formation of primary and secondary air pollutants including tropospheric ozone, NOx, SOx, aerosols, and VOCs; Air pollution control strategies and technologies; Impacts of air pollution on health and environment; Stratospheric ozone destruction; Global climate change.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 3121 , or ME 302 and ME 312.

courses.title: Safe Product Design and Analysis
courses.description: A study of the engineering tools and methods used to design products in such a way as to prevent accidents and injuries from occurring, and to establish causation if an accident or injury does occur. Major tools discussed include: the use of industry standards and government regulations, warnings and labels, Fault Tree Analysis (FTA), and Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA). Failure analysis case studies from real cases, as well as group projects involving the analysis of real commercial products are utilized to illustrate concepts. Discussion of product liability litigation issues.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 2150 or ME 215, C- or better in ME 3150 or ME 315, and C- or better in ME 3190 or ME 319.

courses.title: Entertainment Design Engineering
courses.description: Selection of a compelling story for an amusement park ride, and incorporation of the story into waiting area, ride design, and AR/VR elements. Economic feasibility. Introduction to the design of all elements of the ride including track layout, structural analysis, vehicle design, dynamics, propulsion, and brakes. Passenger safety considerations including collision avoidance, safe accelerations, passenger restraints, clearance envelopes, emergency egress, emergency brake design. Knowledge of finite element analysis (for example ME 4060) is useful, but not necessary.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ME 2150 and C- or better in ME 3190 .

courses.title: Introduction to Micro-Electromechanical Systems
courses.description: An introduction of Micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS), which is the integration of mechanical elements, sensors, actuators, and electronics with a dimension of micrometers. It has been found increased application in a variety of industrial areas including; semi-conductors, automation, and biomedical fields. Exploration of various aspects of MEMS, including materials, design, fabrication and applications of MEMS. Top-level survey of MEMS encompassing broad coverage of this multidisciplinary field.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ME 3150 or ME 315, ME 3121 or ME 312, ME 4351 or ME 435, and ME 4351L or ME 435L.
